transcript.text: A dryer that seems not to stop can be normal on a timed cycle or during an anti-crease/cool-down phase, but an automatic programme that keeps running with dry clothes can point to dirty moisture-sensor strips or, less commonly, a timer/control fault. First check whether the programme is timed or sensor/automatic, and whether the displayed time or dial position is actually changing. If it is a sensor programme, switch it off and unplug it, then wipe the two metal sensor strips inside the drum with a cloth lightly dampened with white vinegar; conditioner residue can stop them sensing dryness. Is it on a timed or automatic programme, and does its time/setting stay unchanged while it runs?
its finished, display says End but the drum keeps turning for a bit every few mins. dont know if its timed or automatic

That sounds like the normal anti-crease (or crease-care) phase. Once the display shows “End”, many dryers briefly turn the drum every few minutes to stop the clothes settling into creases; it should not be reheating or actively drying at that point. It normally stops by itself after a set period, which varies by make and programme. If it carries on for several hours, starts heating again, or the drum turns continuously despite showing End, switch it off and arrange an engineer, as that would suggest a control fault.
ok but how long does it go on for? worried its wasting electricity

Usually it is up to around 1–2 hours after “End”, although the exact time varies by dryer and crease-care option. Because it only turns briefly every few minutes, it uses very little electricity compared with the heating part of a drying cycle; it should not be heating during this phase. You can switch the dryer off at the controls, or unplug it once it has finished, if you do not want the anti-crease action. If it is still intermittently turning after roughly two hours, turns continuously, or feels warm/heats again after showing End, that is not normal and would point to a control fault needing an engineer.
